chunks: Sa'd narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn al-Saqr, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Lu'lu'i, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Do we give a man from the zakat one hundred dirhams?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'Two hundred?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'Three hundred?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'Four hundred?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'Five hundred?' He said, 'Yes,' until he enrich him.
ai.seo_question: What is the minimum amount of zakat given to a single poor person according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that there is no fixed minimum threshold for zakat distribution to an individual, as long as the amount suffices to alleviate their poverty. The term 'enrich' (yughnihi) is interpreted by Shia jurists not as creating permanent wealth, but as providing sufficient resources to meet immediate needs or achieve financial independence from ongoing charity. This flexibility underscores the pragmatic and compassionate nature of zakat in Shia fiqh, prioritizing the actual relief of the recipient over rigid numerical constraints.
